'''''Silene flos-cuculi''''' (syn. ''Lychnis flos-cuculi''), the '''ragged-robin''', is a perennial herbaceous plant in the family [[Caryophyllaceae]].{{r|powo}}{{r|bsbi}} It is native to Eurasia and Siberia <ref>{{cite web|url=https://powo.science.kew.org/taxon/urn:lsid:ipni.org:names:911444-1|website=powo.science.kew.org|title=Silene flos-cuculi (L.) Greuter & Burdet |publisher=[[Royal Botanic Gardens, Kew|Royal Botanical Gardens Kew]]|access-date=29 March 2025}}</ref> and has been introduced to North America.

==Description==
[[File:Lychnis flos-cuculi L. in Botanica in originali.jpg|left|thumb|242x242px|"Lychnis flos-cuculi" in ''Botanica in Originali'', by [[Johann Hieronymus Kniphof]]]]
''Silene flos-cuculi'' forms a rosette of low growing foliage with numerous stems {{Convert|30 to 90|cm|abbr=off|frac=2}} tall. The stems rise above the foliage and branch near the top of the stem.<ref name="Nor"/> The leaves are paired, with the lower leaves spoon-shaped and stalked.{{cn|date=March 2025}} The middle and upper leaves are linear-lanceolate with pointed apexes. All of the leaves are untoothed. The stems have barbed hairs pointing downward and these hairs make the plant rough to the touch.<ref name="Nor">{{cite book |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=NURmQDm_dJsC&pg=PA185 |page=185 |title=Flora of North America: Volume 5: Magnoliophyta: Caryophyllidae, Part 2 |author=Flora of North America Editorial Committee |publisher=OUP USA |year=1993 |isbn=978-0-19-522211-1 }}</ref>

Blooming from May to August (and occasionally later), the pink flowers are {{cvt|3 to 4|cm}} wide. They have five narrow petals deeply divided into four lobes giving the flower an untidy, ragged appearance, hence its common name. The [[sepal|calyx]] tube is five-toothed with ten [[stamen]]s. There are 5 separate styles.<ref name="Harrap2013">{{cite book |last1=Harrap |first1=Simon |title=Harrap's Wild Flowers |date=2013 |publisher=Bloomsbury |location=London |isbn=9781472966483 |pages=415 |edition=1}}</ref>{{rp|154}}

The fruits consist of small (6 to 10 mm) capsules opening on top by five teeth and containing many small seeds; they are found on the plants from August onward.

== Distribution and habitat ==
The species is native to Europe and Asia,{{r|powo}} where it is found along roads and in [[wet meadow]]s and pastures. It has also become naturalized in parts of the northern United States and eastern Canada.{{r|usda}}

== Ecology ==
[[File:Käokannid.JPG|thumb|A population of ragged robin in Estonia]]
Butterflies and long-tongued bees feed on the flowers' nectar. In addition to these pollinators, the flowers are visited by many types of insects, and can be characterized by a generalized [[pollination syndrome]].<ref>{{Cite journal |doi=10.1111/plb.12328 |title=Competition for pollinators and intra-communal spectral dissimilarity of flowers |journal=Plant Biology |pages=56–62 |year=2015 |last1=Van Der Kooi |first1=C. J. |last2=Pen |first2=I. |last3=Staal |first3=M. |last4=Stavenga |first4=D. G. |last5=Elzenga |first5=J. T. M. |url=https://pure.rug.nl/ws/files/78585910/Competition_for_pollinators_and_intra_communal_spectral_dissimilarity_of_flowers.pdf |pmid=25754608 |volume=18 |issue=1 |archive-date=16 November 2023 |access-date=21 December 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231116182426/https://pure.rug.nl/ws/files/78585910/Competition_for_pollinators_and_intra_communal_spectral_dissimilarity_of_flowers.pdf |url-status=live }}</ref>

In Britain it has declined in numbers because of modern farming techniques and draining of wet-lands and is no longer common.

==Cultivation==
Popular garden [[cultivar]]s include:
* 'Alba' – white-flowered form
* {{tdes|Jenny}} = 'Lychjen'<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.rhs.org.uk/Plants/194188/Lychnis-flos-cuculi-Jenny-Lychjen-(d)/Details |title=''Lychnis flos-cuculi'' {{tdes|'''Jenny'''}} = 'Lychjen' |publisher=RHS |access-date=4 June 2021 |archive-date=24 June 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210624203455/https://www.rhs.org.uk/Plants/194188/Lychnis-flos-cuculi-Jenny-Lychjen-(d)/Details |url-status=live }}</ref> 
* 'Nana' – dwarf form (4 inches) with smaller leaf rosettes and shorter flower stems
* 'Petite Jenny'<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.rhs.org.uk/Plants/344084/Lychnis-flos-cuculi-Petite-Jenny-(d)/Details |title=''Lychnis flos-cuculi'' 'Petite Jenny' |publisher=RHS |access-date=4 June 2021 }}</ref> 
* 'White Robin'<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.rhs.org.uk/Plants/216347/Lychnis-flos-cuculi-White-Robin/Details |title=''Lychnis flos-cuculi'' 'White Robin' |publisher=RHS |access-date=4 June 2021 }}</ref>
